title: Repair Resources tutorial as one runnable authenticated app and test path
description:
The Resources tutorial does not currently describe one application that a new consumer can build and test through all five chapters. Repair the existing guide as a coherent path; no new Resources API or implicit cache-scope rule is needed.

Verified against research pin 22b2e9951979fb87271f6f2304e628d5aceea454 and current f680007c6b7dcb63cf4dd4bdd7b39f83d8c4c9d4. All 160 source files in the research manifest remained unchanged at final validation.

Concrete defects:

1. docs/resources/tutorial/02-server-data.md:19-26 instructs adding both Resources and managed HTTP, but the dependency map omits day8/re-frame2-http. The namespace at line 60 requires re-frame.http.managed. A detached consumer with exactly the shown dependencies fails to require it; adding only the HTTP artifact succeeds. Preserve the compiler and development alias from setup when showing additive dependency changes, and show the registration namespaces' boot-loading path.
2. Parts 2 and 4 leave article/list/detail reads global after introducing authentication; Part 4 populates the global detail from an authenticated favorite reply. Anonymous readability does not imply viewer-invariant favorited/following/content visibility. Use the reference Conduit's viewer resolver and correct transition/replan/clear behavior when adding auth. Do not classify the correctly scoped reference implementation as broken. A separate deliberately global browser registration reproduced reuse of a prior viewer's synthetic marker after switching to Bob, with no second request.
3. Part 5 says the earlier registration namespaces contain no browser code and can be renamed to .cljc. Part 3 contains unguarded js/globalThis and js/JSON interop. An isolated literal interop form fails JVM compilation with "No such namespace: js". Part 5 also tests :auth/flow, :auth/state and :auth/error machinery not constructed in Part 3, which teaches direct auth handlers. Make the tests exercise the application actually taught, on their stated target, including the view test's namespace/target.
4. The tutorial's .io API base differs from the current official .show API. Provide a concrete local-demo route as well as current hosted configuration. This finding does not assert the old endpoint's live availability.

Acceptance: from a clean consumer, follow the revised setup through a read, refresh failure, authenticated viewer change and favorite mutation, then run the tests taught for that same app. Record every necessary dependency/require, visible state and command outcome. A docs-site build alone cannot establish snippet compilation or runtime behavior. Keep the repair focused on continuity and current idioms rather than converting every small editorial issue into a separate task.

Evidence in the mayor checkout: ai/findings/Resources/astra/report.md and sibling-review.md; evidence/consumer-literal-re-frame2-1.log (exit 1), consumer-repaired-re-frame2-1.log (exit 0), facade-portability-re-frame2-1.log (exit 0 for asserted counterexample), scope-counterexample.json, and local-source-manifest.json. Research fixtures are local ignored artifacts; reproduction and source locations above are included so this bead is actionable without treating them as shipped tests.

DEFECTS, AS REPAIRED
1. HTTP dependency: Part 2's deps map adds day8/re-frame2-http and keeps thheller/shadow-cljs and the :dev alias; Part 1's routing map regains the compiler; Part 2 shows core requiring conduit.resources (boot-loading path); Part 3 adds day8/re-frame2-schemas, which its rf/reg-app-schemas call needs.
2. Viewer scope: introduced in Part 3 ("Whose cache is it? Scope reads by viewer"), at the point requests start carrying a token. conduit.scope registers :conduit/viewer on the reference resolver's model (username -> [:rf.scope/viewer {:username}], blank token -> [:rf.scope/viewer :anonymous], token without user -> nil, fail-closed). Part 2's :conduit/articles and :conduit/article move to {:from-db :conduit/viewer}; the shell shows "Restoring your session…" while :auth/restoring?; both restore outcomes dispatch :rf.route/replan-resources; logout resolves the old scope, dispatches :rf.resource/clear-scope, navigates home, then replans (so signing out while already on home still loads the anonymous list). Part 2 keeps :rf.scope/global and states why (no request carries a credential yet). Part 4 adds :conduit/session and the :conduit/feed registration, extends logout to clear both scopes, and every mutation example uses viewer/session descriptors.
3. Portability and tests: Part 3's three browser touches (JSON.parse, and localStorage in the persist fx and token cofx) are behind #?(:cljs …), with Cheshire on the JVM for the parse; registration files are .cljc from their parts (api, resources, scope, auth, mutations, views). Part 5 tests Part 3's direct handlers against conduit.api (no :auth/flow/state/error), exercises the JVM JSON branch with a real 422 body, and moves the view test to test/conduit/views_test.clj on the portable view, under {:preset :test :rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live}, asserting the write settles :success in that frame (the old some? assertion could not fail).
4. API base: https://api.realworld.show/api, plus a local route — the upstream reference backend (nitro-prisma-zod-realworld-example-app, Bun, make setup, http://localhost:3000/api). The in-repo demo backend is not offered to consumers: it has no deps manifest to depend on, and it has a single demo user, so it cannot show a viewer switch. No claim about the old .io host.

Also broken on the walked path and fixed: Part 3's reg-app-schemas ran with no frame at ns load (now rf/with-frame :rf/default) and its non-:maybe slices rejected every boot write (now [:maybe FormSlice]); :auth/user sub was missing; shell wiring for login and sign-out was absent; Part 4 required undefined conduit.http and conduit.schema; Part 5's text-content value was "  7" but is " 7".
